title: Client Services Desk Guidance: Several Microsoft 365 Subscriptions in One Tenant
content:
**Rule.** A client's single Microsoft 365 tenant may carry any number of Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) subscriptions. These can be different plans, or the same plan on different terms or billing frequencies. Each subscription holds one plan on one term, with its own term dates, price and cancellation window.

**No pooling.** Licenses of different subscriptions are never pooled for pricing, proration, refunds or renewal. Each subscription is decided on its own records. The only rule that adds licenses up across subscriptions is the tenant-wide plan license cap.

## What this means at the desk

| Question about a tenant's subscriptions | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a limit on how many subscriptions one client may hold? | No. There is no per-client subscription limit. |
| May one tenant hold the same plan twice, for example once on P1M and once on P1Y? | Yes. Each is a separate subscription with its own term, price and window. |
| Do two subscriptions' licenses combine to reach a proration, refund or renewal figure? | No. Each subscription is figured from its own records. |
| Which rule adds the subscriptions together? | Only the tenant-wide plan license cap. |

**Illustration (hypothetical holdings).** A tenant holds 40 Microsoft 365 Business Premium licenses on a P1Y subscription billed annually, and 15 on a P1M subscription. The two subscriptions have separate unit prices, term end dates and cancellation windows. A reduction or a refund on one of them is worked out from that subscription alone. The 55 licenses are counted together only when the tenant-wide cap for Microsoft 365 Business Premium is tested.
